public_rationale: Cursor announced that SpaceX completed its acquisition on August 14, 2026. Cursor is one of the AI startups discussed in the post. That completed transaction contradicts the categorical forecast that none could get acquired or go public. It does not establish profitability or improving margins.
limitations: This is an event-based verdict, not a financial verdict. The unspecified accounting basis prevents scoring the profitability and margin premises.
The combined claim should be split if the register requires one verdict covering every financial premise as well as the exit forecast.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Every AI company is unprofitable with worsening margins as it scales, so none will be able to get acquired or go public.

statement.excerpt: I believe every AI company is unprofitable with margins that are getting increasingly worse as they scale, and as a result that none of them will be able to either get acquired or go public.

from_speaker: margins that are getting increasingly worse as they scale
none of them will be able to either get acquired or go public
our_interpretation: The relevant companies are AI-focused startups, including AI application companies discussed in the post. Diversified technology companies and chip suppliers are excluded.
The forecast makes a categorical claim about completed acquisitions and IPOs. One completed acquisition or IPO after publication disproves that component.
The profitability and margin statements are financial premises. Their accounting basis and margin measure are unspecified; they cannot receive a separate financial verdict.
The proposed verdict concerns the categorical exit forecast, not whether the financial premises were true.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes the asserted financial conditions and the permanent impossibility of acquisitions or IPOs throughout the relevant population. A period without exits is insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one relevant AI startup completes an acquisition or IPO after the post and by the evaluation date.
